title: Q (worked example): Determine which of the two angle bisectors is acute for 3x + 4y − 5 = 0 and 5x + 12y + 13 = 0
notes: Both constants (−5 and +13) — the second line already has a positive constant; for the first, multiply through by −1 so the constant is positive: −3x − 4y + 5 = 0, giving a₁ = −3, b₁ = −4
For the second line: a₂ = 5, b₂ = 12
Since this is negative, the **(+) sign bisector is the acute angle bisector**, and the (−) sign bisector is the obtuse angle bisector
